explanations.1: This is where you put the email address for whoever manages the system—it's used to send important notifications.
explanations.2: This is a secret password-like token that proves the admin is really the admin; make it long and random so it's hard to guess.
explanations.4: This random string is mixed with user IP addresses before hashing them, so even if two systems hash the same IP, they get different results.
explanations.5: This secret string prevents attackers from forging security tokens by mixing it into the token creation process.
